title: Performance Orbit: Unified per-model & per-route dashboard with cost-aware chart specs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a compact, scannable Performance Orbit view in the Redwood Console that surfaces per-model and per-route latency, throughput, token composition, and cost signals. This ticket consolidates chart-level specs, interaction patterns for drilldowns and rollouts, and a hi-fidelity prototype for stakeholder review. The goal is to enable engineers and SREs to identify regressions quickly, understand cost drivers per 1K tokens, and evaluate canary/rollout health without switching screens.
design_goals: Surface 95th/99th latency bands alongside p50 so regression signals are obvious
Show throughput (req/s) and concurrency over the same time axis for correlation
Display token-level breakdown (prompt vs generated vs tool calls) with a compact sankey/spark representation
Expose immediate cost impact (cost per 1K tokens and cost delta by model variant) in-line with performance charts
Enable rapid comparison between model variants and routes using a temporary overlay
Support quick pivot to timeline traces and request sample set for debugging
Accessible color palette and keyboard interactions for chart focus and tooltips
ux_flow: Entry: User lands on Performance Orbit for a selected model or route (route selector at top-left)
Top row: Key metric cards (p50 latency, p95 latency, p99 latency, throughput, cost/1K) with small sparklines
Mid row: Combined timeline (Latency Halo) showing percentile bands with throughput pathline superimposed; hover reveals percentile dropdown and quick link to traces
Right column: Variant Ribbon comparing two pinned variants side-by-side with delta badges and a confidence indicator
Bottom row: Token Orbit — stacked, normalized token composition with mini-sankey linking prompt->generated->tool-call; clicking a slice opens sample requests filtered
Canary/rollout overlay: When a rollout is active, show canary band with sample rate slider and automated anomaly marker explanations
Actions: Export CSV, Open traces, Create incident, Pin chart to dashboard, Start A/B comparison
chart_specs: Latency Halo: Area bands for p50/p75/p95/p99 with translucent layering; x-axis = time (1m granularity by default), y-axis = latency (ms) on log scale; overlay: throughput as thin monotone line; interaction: brush to select time-range and link to traces; annotation layer supports autosynced rollout events

Throughput Pathline: Dual-axis chart with left axis requests/sec (area) and right axis concurrency (line); supports smoothing toggle and sample markers for large spikes; tooltip shows avg tokens/request at that point

Token Orbit (stacked-sankey compact): Represents token composition over time as small multiple rows; encoding: height = total tokens, color = category (prompt/generated/tool); interaction: tap to filter requests, long-press for request example; aggregates: sum and median tokens per request

Cost Compass: Small radial/comparison widget showing cost per 1K tokens for selected model variant and baseline; delta shown as percent and absolute USD; clicking opens cost breakdown table (model compute, quantization overhead, I/O)

Variant Ribbon: Side-by-side small multiples for latency and cost with normalized sparkline, delta pill, and confidence band computed from bootstrapped samples; interaction: 'Pin to compare' turns selection into overlay on main charts

Percentile Waterfall: Bar view that shows distribution of token-level latency contributions (token index buckets) for a selected request cohort; helpful for diagnosing long-tail token stalls; includes adjustable bucket size
Microtrace Swimlane: Compact row per sampled request with time-aligned events (queue, kernel-exec, kv-fetch, tool-call); clicking a swimlane opens full trace in Flame UI
Heatline Correlation Matrix: Small matrix of correlation coefficients between metrics (latency, throughput, tokens, cost); hover reveals scatter preview and regression line
feedback: 2026-02-22 - PM review (Priya Desai): ask to surface SLA breach badge on key metric cards and include action buttons for emergency rollbacks
2026-02-27 - Eng review (Arjun Patel): requested ability to toggle log vs linear y-axis for latency and suggested adding autoscaling event annotations
2026-03-03 - SRE session (Janelle Ruiz): prefer default time window = 30m for live traffic, 24h for historical; recommended sampling limits for microtraces to avoid overload
2026-03-10 - Design critique (Ava Morgan): visual language for variant ribbon needs stronger affordance for pinned comparisons; accessibility check requested for colorblind palettes
2026-03-11 - Legal/Compliance (Diego Flores): ensure prototype does not surface raw request text by default; sample viewer must redact PII and include consent link
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates all 7 chart types in active state with mock data
Hover, brush, pin, and filter interactions are documented and reproducible in the prototype
Cost Compass includes USD breakdown and links to billing dashboard
Canary overlay shows sample rate slider and annotates automatic anomalies
Accessibility: color contrast passes WCAG AA for main charts and keyboard navigation can access tooltips and pins
Engineering sign-off on data feasibilty (ENG owner assigned) and clear performance budget for frontend rendering
next_steps: Incorporate feedback from PM and Eng and update figma assets (due 2026-03-16)
Add sample redaction flow to prototype and confirm with Legal (owner: Lucas)
Schedule joint review with ENG runtime team to validate percentile sources and trace links (target 2026-03-18)
Prepare handoff packet for implementation including static SVG assets and interaction specs
notes: Trade-offs discussed: full sankey for tokens is expensive to render on high-cardinality routes; opted for compact stacked-sankey with expand-on-demand
Performance: prefer canvas-backed rendering for timeline and seaborn-like downsampling for 1m->5s aggregation bursts
Security: sample viewer must default to redacted mode and require explicit opt-in to view raw prompts
UX pattern: use a persistent route selector and ephemeral compare mode to avoid cluttering single-route view
